mostWorthwhile.text: Filtering blood and then recovering useful substances was most worthwhile: the picture plans distinguish what enters the tubule from what returns to blood, including glucose and water.

leastWorthwhile.text: Attaching the ureters and bladder was clear but relatively repetitive after the earlier urine-drainage picture had already shown their route.

surprise.text: The emphasis on filtering useful glucose and then recovering almost all of it clarified that filtration is not simply the removal of waste.

arbitrary.text: The separate water-permeable tubule felt somewhat like a construction piece added to an existing nephron; the result shows water returning but does not explain what drives that movement.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: tracing filtration and recovery into the body's circulation was a useful way to connect cellular transport with organ function, despite the predictable assembly steps.
